reading.text: The first interior is closed overhead by one continuous curved surface that gathers everything beneath it toward a single opening at the crown. The second is closed by a repeated element: a series of transverse arches that divide the ceiling into bays and carry the eye along the room rather than up into it. In the first, a ring of engaged columns stands against the drum below the springing, and the coffering above diminishes in scale as it rises. In the second, nothing diminishes; the bays are equal and the rhythm is flat. The two rooms are doing the same work — closing a large volume — by opposite means, and the difference is legible in the ceiling alone.
